reason: The default deferral and the auto/10% threshold are stated as written. The model requirement is incomplete: on Google Cloud's Agent Platform tool search needs Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 4.5 or later, and it is never used on Microsoft Foundry deployments hosted on Azure or with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS or HIPAA configurations. The unqualified 'requires Sonnet 4, Opus 4 or Haiku 4.5 and later' therefore overstates where it applies. A search also turned up an older Agent SDK page saying Haiku models don't support tool search, but the current MCP page lists Haiku 4.5.
found: Claude Code uses tool search on Claude Opus 4, Claude Sonnet 4, Claude Haiku 4.5, and later models, or Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, and later models on Google Cloud's Agent Platform. ... Tool search isn't supported on Microsoft Foundry deployments hosted on Azure
suggested_fix: In Claude Code, MCP tool search is enabled by default, so MCP tool definitions are deferred. ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto loads them upfront while their definitions stay under 10% of the context window. Tool search runs on Claude Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Haiku 4.5 and later (4.5 and later on Google Cloud's Agent Platform) and is not available on Microsoft Foundry deployments hosted on Azure.

reason: The page states the 50,000-character persist-to-file threshold for successful text results, says MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS doesn't change it, and gives the 500,000-character ceiling for anthropic/maxResultSizeChars.
found: Unless the server raises a tool's own limit, successful text results longer than 50,000 characters are saved to a file regardless of this variable. ... Claude Code raises that tool's threshold to the annotated value, up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters.

reason: The hooks reference states all three points: updatedToolOutput replaces the result Claude sees, the tool has already run when the hook fires, and OpenTelemetry tool spans capture the original output.
found: updatedToolOutput only changes what Claude sees. The tool has already run by the time the hook fires ... Telemetry such as OpenTelemetry tool spans and analytics events also captures the original output before the hook runs.

reason: The sandboxing page says the operating system enforces the boundary, that it restricts filesystem and network access, and that it is off by default and turned on with /sandbox or sandbox.enabled.
found: The Bash sandbox is a boundary that the operating system enforces around the shell commands Claude runs ... You set which files and network domains those commands can reach ... The sandbox is off by default. To turn it on, run /sandbox in a session ... or set sandbox.enabled to true

reason: The sources support these points: it is a Messages API feature (not available in Managed Agents), it uses allowed_callers with code_execution_20260120 or later, Haiku 4.5 is excluded, MCP connector tools are excluded, and modelUsage is recommended over usage when subagents run. No cited source says it is 'not a Claude Code setting'. That is an inference from the absence of any mention in the Claude Code docs, and a search found no explicit statement either way.
found: Feature of Messages API ... Programmatic tool calling requires the code execution tool with tool version code_execution_20260120 or later. Claude Haiku 4.5 ... doesn't support programmatic tool calling. ... The following tools cannot be called programmatically: Tools provided by an MCP connector
suggested_fix: Programmatic tool calling is a Messages API feature (allowed_callers with code_execution_20260120 or later); the Claude Code docs reviewed do not describe a setting for it. Claude Haiku 4.5 does not support it, and tools from an MCP connector cannot be called programmatically. For Agent SDK token accounting, use modelUsage, because the usage field undercounts once subagents run.
